text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
CAPITAL
- Romania needs clear banking laws in order if it wants to put order in the banking sector, central bank governor Mugur Isarescu says in interview.
- Private farmers are reluctant to get fresh credits, even with low interest rates, the paper says.
ADEVARUL
- The Health Ministry plans to cut prices of imported medicines.
- The government ordered state-run companies to pay their old debts to the budget to solve financial bottlenecks.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The commission in charge of fighting corruption recouped 448 billion lei lost to tax evasion.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Reform Minister Ulm Spineanu asked the state Tarom SA airline to stop using its ageing fleet of Soviet-made AN-24s.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Lack of funds forced Romania last year to irrigate only 20 percent of its cropland, the paper says.
- Procter&Gamble will invest $50 million in a detergent factory in the western city of Timisoara.
- Sales of the locally-made Dacia car dropped by 23 percent since March, the paper says.
- Turnover at the Bucharest stock exchange hit a record 11 billion lei over the past week.
- The local leu currency fell slightly at retail shops, the paper says.
- The Agricultural Bank SA commercial bank gave credits worth 242 billion lei to the farming sector this year.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- The government decided to cut the road taxes proposed by the transport ministry.
